**Disputed — flagged for the expert.** The fixture files this under 2.5.3 as "a field whose only label is its placeholder", but on the criterion's own terms 2.5.3 is satisfied here: the visible text is the placeholder "Email" and the accessible name computed from that placeholder is "Email", so the name does contain the visible label. The real defects on this element are 3.3.2 (no persistent label — the text vanishes as soon as the user types) and arguably 4.1.2. It is also expected to be never-captured, because the label rule skips a control with no visible text and an <input type="email"> has none. Recorded as a pass under 2.5.3 rather than deleted, so the disagreement is visible and can be adjudicated.

rationale: The button reads "Renew" and its aria-label is "Renew all loans". The name contains the visible text, so the letter of 2.5.3 is met and a voice command matches. But the name widens the scope the visible text promised — "Renew" on its own does not tell a sighted user that pressing it renews every item — so the two audiences are told different things about what the control does. That is a real problem and it is not the one 2.5.3 measures. Uncertain is the calibrated answer.
